Illustration: a hospital isotope laboratory. On a wooden table is a thick-walled lead shield, inside which is a small glass vial of radioactive medicine. Above the vial floats an enlarged group of nuclei: some are orange and undecayed, some are grey rings, that is, already decayed, and a ray is just leaving two of them. Next to it is a radiation meter whose probe points at the vial and whose needle trembles. On the wall is a clock.
Kolme ruudukkoa vierekkäin: samat 100 ra: Three grids side by side: the same 100 radioactive nuclei at three moments. An undecayed nucleus is an orange filled circle, a decayed nucleus a grey ring. At the time t = 0 all 100 are undecayed. After one half-life 52 are undecayed and after two half-lives 28. The decayed nuclei are in random places of the grid, and neither the place nor the age of a nucleus predicts its decay.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: hajoamattomien yt: Graph to scale: the number N of undecayed nuclei as a function of time. On the horizontal axis the time in half-lives from zero to five, on the vertical axis N, the scale from zero to the initial number N zero in quarters. The curve starts from the value N zero and falls ever more gently. Dashed lines show that at one half-life a half of the initial number is left, at two a quarter and at three an eighth. The curve never reaches zero.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, simuloitu esimerk: Graph to scale, simulated example data: the number of pulses of a barium-137m sample in periods of 10 seconds as a function of time, time from zero to 900 seconds, 16 data points at intervals of 60 seconds. In the first period there are 249 pulses, and the number decreases exponentially towards the level of the background radiation, about 5 pulses in 10 seconds. A fitted curve A times e to the power minus C t plus B is drawn through the points, and the level B of the background radiation is a horizontal dashed line. The points are on both sides of the curve.

Graph to scale, simulated example data: the number of pulses of a protactinium-234m sample in periods of 10 seconds as a function of time, time from zero to 400 seconds, 21 data points at intervals of 20 seconds. The points are the same as in the table of the task: 380 pulses at the start, about 10 pulses at the end. No fit is drawn in the figure.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: tuntemattoman rad: Graph to scale: the activity of an unknown radioactive sample in kilobecquerels as a function of time, time from zero to 20 hours, grid spacing 1 hour and 50 kilobecquerels. The activity is 720 kilobecquerels at the start and decreases ever more gently.
